test_title: PYST 59: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 23 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following correctly describes parenchyma, a simple permanent tissue?

options.text: Parenchyma consists of dead, thick-walled cells without intercellular spaces.
Parenchyma is made of living, loosely arranged cells with thin walls that store food.
Parenchyma is a complex tissue found only in vascular bundles.
Parenchyma cells are highly specialised and tightly packed with no space between them.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Parenchyma is made of living, loosely arranged cells with thin walls that store food**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parenchyma** is the most common and fundamental type of **simple permanent tissue** found in plants.
 
• It consists of **living cells** that possess **thin cell walls** usually made of **cellulose**. They are generally **isodiametric** in shape, meaning they have approximately equal diameters in all directions.
 
• The cells are typically **loosely arranged**, which results in significant **intercellular spaces** between them. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct and statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• Unlike **sclerenchyma**, which consists of dead cells with thickened lignified walls, **parenchyma** cells remain **metabolically active** throughout their life. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Parenchyma** is a **simple tissue** because it is composed of only **one type of cell** that is similar in structure and function. It is not a **complex tissue** like **Xylem** or **Phloem**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The primary **functions** of parenchyma include **food storage**, providing **turgidity** for mechanical support, and **secretion**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Specialized Parenchyma:**
 
 
• **Chlorenchyma**: When **parenchyma** contains **chloroplasts** and performs **photosynthesis**, it is called **chlorenchyma**. This is primarily found in the **mesophyll** of leaves.
 
• **Aerenchyma**: In **aquatic plants** (hydrophytes), large **air cavities** are present in the **parenchyma** to provide **buoyancy**, allowing the plant to float. This variation is known as **aerenchyma**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with other Simple Tissues:**
 
 
• **Collenchyma**: These cells are **living** and **elongated** with **unevenly thickened corners** due to the deposition of **cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin**. They provide **flexibility** and **mechanical strength** to young stems and **petioles**.
 
• **Sclerenchyma**: These are **dead cells** at maturity, characterized by **highly thickened walls** containing **lignin**. They provide **stiffness** and **rigidity** to plant parts, such as the **husk of a coconut**.
 
 
 
• **Location**: **Parenchyma** is distributed throughout the plant body, including the **pith**, **cortex** of roots and stems, **mesophyll** of leaves, and the **flesh of fruits**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Simple vs. Complex Tissues**: **Simple tissues** (Parenchyma, Collenchyma, Sclerenchyma) consist of **homogeneous cells**. **Complex tissues** (Xylem and Phloem) consist of **heterogeneous cells** (different types of cells working together as a unit).
 
• **Cell Wall Composition**: The **thin walls** of **parenchyma** allow for the easy exchange of materials and **osmosis**. In **storage parenchyma**, the walls may store **hemicellulose** as a reserve food material.
 
• **Regeneration**: Because **parenchyma** cells are **living** and maintain the ability to **divide** (totipotency), they play a crucial role in **wound healing** and **regeneration** in plants.
 
• **Date of Discovery**: The term **Parenchyma** was coined by **Nehemiah Grew** in the **17th century**, who is often referred to as the **Father of Plant Anatomy**.
</ul
